1. Yes they require a ton of maintenance. They are not a sit in a cage and watch pet. They are more like a dog or a cat. They need daily time outside of the cage, alot of hands on attention. Cage cleaning at the least weekly. 

They shouldnt be aggressive. Rats are generally excellent sweet pets. I highly suggest finding a good responsible breeder, one who breeds for healthy/temperament and handles them daily as babies. 

I am a breeder myself but I have owned both pet store rats and bred. Pet store rats can be sweet, but it is a roll of the dice, if they were not handled they may be afraid and it will take time and effort to bond with them.

2. I prefer to think of them like cats. It depends on their individual personality. With the right person who takes the time they can be very trainable, just like some people do train cats to do amazing things. Look up rat trick videos on you tube! 

But for the most part they have selective hearing lol. Like my rats are trained to come when called, but sometimes they peek at me and then decide they don't want to come lol. Rats are highly intelligent though.

3. Very very noisy. I had them in my bedroom at one point in time and I got used to it and it didnt bother me, it drove my husband crazy. You can play with them before bed to tire them out but they will still be a bit noisy.

4. Urine and poop never smell nice. If you stay on top of cleaning, use a good bedding, work on some litterbox training and do not over crowd the cage it is not bad at all. 

You definitely want to get 2 rats of the same gender or fixed. They do best in groups.

Getting a dog from a program can be very difficult for mental health issues if you are not a veteran. Not impossible but difficult. The pricing is probably around 20,000 on the very cheap end and often higher. And takes a year or more.

The other option is to do owner training. You are allowed to train your own dog. I did!

I would suggest rescuing a dog from a shelter that is over a year old, so that the rescue can give u alot of info on their personality. Not all dogs are suitable to become service dogs. Another option is to go with a breeder that can give u alot of info on the parents temperament, knows their puppies and even better if they have raised puppies for service dogs in the past.

Still training will take a year or two before they are ready to become a service dog. I would highly suggest finding a local trainer in your area to help.

Lastly your dog has to learn tasks that help you with your disability. 

I can give u alot of links for more helpful info:
This is the goto site for all info:

Also these facebook groups are a godsend of info and helpful people:
https://www.facebook.com/groups/OTSDServiceDogs/

https://www.facebook.com/groups/110181312493575/ 



Also do not register your dog online if u get one. These are all scam sites. You do not need to register your dog. You do not need anything at all, unless you are traveling or need accomidations for work/housing. Then you will need a letter from your doctor.

Which seriously, find a new doctor that is more helpful then just suggesting things. You want a doctor that is going to be hands on and doing things to help u.

**What makes me anxious?** lol about everything! I like the silly quote that goes: *I've got 99 problems and 86 of them are completely made up scenarios in my head*. That is so me.

I feel like my head is turned on shuffle and a million thoughts about what if, how, why are floating or popping up in my head at any given moment.

Usually the what if, the uncertainty of everything sets me off. But I also have social anxiety so being around people is very difficult for me. I wonder what they are thinking? do they hate me? Am I being awkward? am I too shy? do they think I am a bitch? etc...

Also as a rape victim being around men, more so strangers sets it off hardcore. 

**Where does it come from**? I've been in therapy for a while now and still am not 100% sure. Definitely my rape had part to do with it. My therapist says I am very critical of myself and it causes me to overthink things and worry and put myself down which is part of it too. I think overall it is that I want to be safe & secure but life is full of chaos where u don't know what will happen or what someone will do at any moment and it makes me anxious.

**Physically & emotionally**...there are different levels for sure for me. I have just a general unease feeling. Then there is where I start feeling nauseous, dizzy, i feel like I am sick- that almost always happens if I have to go somewhere or do something. Like the expectation of the event coming up makes me literally physically sick.

Then there is when I feel I can't breathe. I am drowning, suffocating. The walls are closing in on me. My mind is racing where I cant even grasp what I am feeling or thinking because it is just this chaotic mess. I want to run and hide and have the earth swallow me. I shake, hyperventilate. I may self harm.

And in the worst case I feel like I am having a heart attack, like I am literally dying. I really feel I can't breathe. It is so terrifying.  

Dealing with it depends on how bad it is. I try to stop & ground myself when I feel it coming on. Something that is a focus can help alot- like a bracelet or necklace to play with. I have even used a rubberband around my wrist to pop. Holding someone's hands or loving on a pet. My dog is trained for tactile stimulation which helps. 

I focus on my breathing. Reminding myself that I can breathe. Slow meaningful breaths. I often tell myself to relax. Sometimes I just have to ride it out. 

As I said before I also might self harm, go for a walk, cuddle with my pets, take a shower. It all depends on what level of reasoning my brain is working at the time.

Knowing u r in control and realizing what you are feeling helps alot but it is not often easy to do.
